answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit if independent audits show fabricated work. Because creating names is cheap but acquiring and locking tokens is not, a sybil attacker must tie up real capital for every fake identity and risks losing it; splitting one stake across many names does not multiply voting weight. A velvet opal in a garden may be a memorable example, but it earns no extra trust.
